record.paper_title: Open Problems in Efficient Semi-Supervised PAC Learning
record.original_question: Consider co-training in which the hypothesis class C is the class of disjunctions, each unlabeled example is a pair (x1, x2) of points in {0,1}^n, the classifier predicts using h(x1), and compatibility requires h(x1) = h(x2). Equivalently, each unlabeled pair is assumed to consist either of two positive examples or of two negative examples. The open question is whether there is a computationally efficient semi-supervised PAC learning algorithm for this co-training-with-disjunctions model that achieves labeled complexity close to the compatibility-based information-theoretic bound.

evidence.quote: Co-training with disjunctions: This is the “inverse” of the two-sided disjunction problem. Let C be the class of disjunctions, but an example x is a pair of points (x1, x2) in {0, 1}^n. Define h(x) = h(x1) but say that h is compatible with x iff h(x1) = h(x2). That is, under our compatibility assumption, each unlabeled example is either a pair of positive examples or a pair of negative examples. Note that D is now a distribution over pairs.
The high-level question is whether for interesting classes C and notions of compatibility χ, one can learn with this many (or polynomial in this many) labeled examples by efficient algorithms.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Fix $n \ge 1$ and let the instance space be $\{0,1\}^n \times \{0,1\}^n$. Let $C$ be the class of monotone (or general) Boolean disjunctions on $n$ variables; for $h \in C$ and a pair $x = (x_1, x_2)$ define the prediction by $h(x) := h(x_1)$, and say that $h$ is compatible with $x$ iff $h(x_1) = h(x_2)$.

Distributional assumption. Let $D$ be an unknown distribution over $\{0,1\}^n \times \{0,1\}^n$ with the property that there exists a target disjunction $h^* \in C$ that is fully compatible with $D$, i.e. $\Pr_{(x_1,x_2)\sim D}[h^*(x_1) = h^*(x_2)] = 1$. Equivalently, every pair drawn from $D$ consists of two positive examples or of two negative examples (under $h^*$).

Learning model. The learner receives an i.i.d. sample of unlabeled pairs from $D$ together with an i.i.d. labeled sample $(x,h^*(x))$ from $D$. Given parameters $\varepsilon, \delta \in (0,1)$, the learner must output, with probability at least $1-\delta$, a hypothesis $\hat h$ such that $\Pr_{(x_1,x_2)\sim D}[\hat h(x_1) \ne h^*(x_1)] \le \varepsilon$.

Information-theoretic baseline. Let $m^*(\varepsilon,\delta,n)$ denote the labeled sample complexity achievable (ignoring computation) by restricting to disjunctions consistent with the unlabeled pairs (i.e., disjunctions $h$ for which $h(x_1)=h(x_2)$ for all observed unlabeled pairs) and applying standard compatibility-based PAC bounds.

Question. Does there exist a learning algorithm running in time $\mathrm{poly}(n,1/\varepsilon,1/\delta)$ that uses $\mathrm{poly}(m^*(\varepsilon,\delta,n))$ labeled examples (and $\mathrm{poly}(n,1/\varepsilon,1/\delta)$ unlabeled pairs) and that, with probability at least $1-\delta$, outputs a hypothesis with error at most $\varepsilon$ in the model above?
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work by Balcan and Zhang (ICML 2013, "Efficient Semi-supervised and Active Learning of Disjunctions") gives efficient semi-supervised and active learning algorithms for disjunctions under natural compatibility/regularity assumptions introduced in the original open-problems paper, addressing the disjunctions co-training setting at least partially. Whether the precise information-theoretic compatibility-based labeled-sample bound is matched by an efficient algorithm in this exact co-training-with-disjunctions formulation is not unambiguously settled in the literature found.

status_evidence.title: Efficient Semi-supervised and Active Learning of Disjunctions
status_evidence.snippet: We provide efficient algorithms for learning disjunctions in the semi-supervised setting under a natural regularity assumption introduced by (Balcan & Blum, 2005).
status_evidence.claim: Efficient semi-supervised algorithms for disjunctions exist under the compatibility/regularity notion from the open-problems paper, providing a partial resolution.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems in Efficient Semi-Supervised PAC Learning
status_evidence.snippet: Open problems including co-training with disjunctions are posed.
status_evidence.claim: The original problem statement appears as an open problem.
